title: The && operator does not evaluate its right side when the left is FALSE

source.quote: returns FALSE if any of the arguments is FALSE
source.supports: one FALSE argument settles the result

source.quote: The function evaluates the arguments until the first TRUE argument, then returns TRUE .
source.supports: the same short-circuit is documented for OR only

derivation: The left side is 7 < 0, FALSE, which settles the result. By symmetry with OR, which is documented to stop at the first TRUE, && stops at the first FALSE and ERROR is not evaluated.
alternative: Short-circuit evaluation is documented for OR, not for AND or &&. If && evaluates both sides, the query fails with the error "right side".
